title: Get to Know Rewild: A Q&A Guide to the 2027 Colormix® Trend Forecast
summary: Get the inside scoop on what sets this year's forecast apart in this Q&A with Emily Kantz, Interior Designer & Color Strategist for Sherwin-Williams.
body_text: Celebrating a return to personal expression through color, this year’s trend forecast features 48 expertly curated hues sought after by designers and forecasted by our Trendsight Team to shape color trends of the future. Moving beyond one-size-fits-all design trends, this Collection encourages homeowners to embrace individuality, drawing inspiration from the pieces, memories and experiences that make their spaces uniquely their own. We sat down with Emily Kantz, Interior Designer & Color Strategist for the Sherwin-Williams Trendsight Team to explore color trends and talk about what sets this year’s forecast apart. What is Rewild and how should I think about using it in my home? A: Rewild is all about a return to creativity and personality in your space. Over the past several years, home design trends leaned heavily into minimalism — clean, neutral palettes that looked beautiful but often felt similar from one home to the next. Now we’re seeing a shift. Homeowners are craving individuality again. They want spaces that feel collected, lived-in and uniquely theirs. That’s where Rewild comes in. It encourages you to start with what you love, whether that’s a vintage find, a piece you picked up while traveling, or something passed down through family, and build your color story from there. These personal items become your “springboard,” helping you reintroduce color, texture and meaning into your home. It’s about embracing imperfection, celebrating personality and letting your space tell your story. How can I confidently mix and match colors without worrying about getting it wrong? A: Rewild is designed to give you freedom, not rules. It gives you 48 hues chosen by experts, so you have the confidence to explore and combine in your own way without having to worry about whether they go together or not. You don’t have to fit into a predefined look. You simply choose colors that resonate with you and work with what you already have in your space. If you have a bold rug, a favorite throw pillow or a standout piece of furniture, pull colors from that. Let those existing elements guide your choices. When your palette is rooted in things you already love, it naturally feels cohesive. The result is a space that feels intentional, approachable and personal because you were part of creating it. Featured Color: Beachcomber SW 9617 What are Continuity Colors and how should I use them? A: Within the 48-color Rewild Collection, there’s a curated group of 10 Continuity Colors . Think of these as your anchors. These shades have been tracked across multiple forecasts because of their versatility and staying power. They’re reliable, adaptable and designed to work across a wide range of spaces and styles. If you’re unsure where to begin, start by ordering free color chip samples to test color in your space. Continuity Colors are: Great for whole-room applications Ideal as foundational wall colors Designed to have a longer lifespan than trend-driven hues From warm neutrals like High Sierra to deeper, moodier tones like Roycroft Bronze Green or Clove , these colors offer a grounded starting point. From there, you can layer in bolder or more playful colors from the rest of the Collection. What’s a simple way to start using Rewild in my home? A: Start with what already exists in your space. Most homes have a primary wall color that flows from room to room. Instead of starting from scratch, look for Rewild colors that complement it: If your current palette leans warm, explore warmer tones like Cordovan or Red Barn If your home has cooler grays or whites, look to colors like Forged Steel or cooler greens From there, introduce color in smaller ways — accent walls, powder rooms, cabinetry or décor. This allows you to experiment without committing to a full room transformation. Featured Colors: Cordovan SW 6027 , White Duck SW 7010 & Quietude SW 6212 What if I feel overwhelmed by all 48 colors? A: That’s completely normal, and exactly why Rewild includes multiple ways to approach the Collection. If you’re feeling unsure, think in terms of mood instead of individual shades. For example: Want something cozy and dramatic? Lean into deeper, moody tones. Looking for something light and playful? Try softer, whimsical hues. Prefer something grounded and natural? Focus on earthy, organic shades. You can also start with a continuity color as your base and build a small palette around it — think 3 to 5 complementary colors from the larger Collection of 48 hues to create a look that feels tied together and cohesive. What’s the biggest shift in how we should think about color today? A: The biggest change is moving away from perfection and toward personalization. Instead of asking, “What’s trending?” the question becomes, “What feels like me?” Rewild invites you to explore, experiment and trust your instincts. It’s less about following a formula and more about building something meaningful. Because at the end of the day, the best color palette isn’t the one that looks perfect online, it’s the one that feels like home. Featured Color: Mauve Finery SW 6282 Ready to bring the Rewild palette into your own space? Get a closer look at the 2027 Colormix® Forecast to explore all 48 colors, uncover design inspiration and discover new ways to express your personal style. Need somewhere simple to start? Order FREE color chips of the 10 Continuity Colors to see these versatile shades in your space before kicking off your color journey.

title: Worthington Enterprises Participating in CJS Securities New Ideas for the New Year Conference
summary: Keep current on Worthington Enterprises’ latest developments and find details about our upcoming schedule of events.
body_text: COLUMBUS, OHIO (January 7, 2026) – Worthington Enterprises (NYSE: WOR), a designer and manufacturer of market-leading brands that improve everyday life by elevating spaces and experiences, today announced that it will participate in next week’s CJS Securities New Ideas for the New Year conference. The virtual presentation is scheduled for Wednesday, January 14 at 8:45 a.m. ET . Please click here to register . President and Chief Executive Officer Joe Hayek and Chief Financial Officer Colin Souza will share the company’s strategy for accelerating growth and shareholder value through the lens of the proven Worthington Business System of innovation, transformation and M&A. A replay of the session will be posted in the Investor Relations section of the Worthington Enterprises website . About Worthington Enterprises Worthington Enterprises (NYSE: WOR) is a designer and manufacturer of market-leading brands that improve everyday life by elevating spaces and experiences. The company operates with two primary business segments: Building Products and Consumer Products. The Building Products segment includes heating and cooling, cooking, construction and water solutions, and building systems including HVAC components, architectural and acoustical grid ceilings and metal framing and accessories. The Consumer Products segment provides solutions for the tools, outdoor living and celebrations categories. Product brands within the Worthington Enterprises portfolio include Balloon Time®, Bernzomatic®, Coleman® (propane cylinders), CoMet®, Elgen, Garden Weasel®, General®, HALO™, Hawkeye™, LEVEL5 Tools®, Mag Torch®, NEXI™, Pactool International®, PowerCore™, Ragasco®, Well-X-Trol® and XLite™, among others. Headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, Worthington Enterprises employs approximately 4,000 people throughout North America and Europe. Founded in 1955 as Worthington Industries, Worthington Enterprises follows a people-first Philosophy with earning money for its shareholders as its first corporate goal. Worthington Enterprises achieves this outcome by empowering its employees to innovate, thrive and grow with leading brands in attractive markets that improve everyday life. The company engages deeply with local communities where it has operations through volunteer efforts and The Worthington Companies Foundation , participates actively in workforce development programs and reports annually on its corporate citizenship and sustainability efforts . For more information, visit worthingtonenterprises.com . title: Financial decisions to revisit as your business grows
summary: Financial priorities evolve as your business grows. Learn how to review cash flow, processes, controls, and risk to stay aligned and plan with confidence.
body_text: Financial decisions to revisit as your business grows July 01, 2026 Business Banking Business Planning Education Fraud Prevention Helpful Tips Small Business As a business grows, financial priorities often evolve. What works in the early stages may not fully support later operations. Over time, transaction volume increases, teams expand, and risk becomes more complex. Because of these changes, it can be helpful to revisit key financial decisions on a regular basis. Doing so can help businesses stay aligned with current needs while also planning ahead with greater confidence. From cash flow to internal controls and risk management, these areas tend to shift gradually. As a result, they are worth reviewing as your business continues to grow. Building a strong financial foundation In the early stages, financial decisions often focus on access and visibility. Typically, a small team manages most responsibilities. While this approach can work initially, building strong habits early can support long-term growth. At the same time, fraud awareness plays an important role in that foundation. Small businesses are often targeted, particularly when safeguards are limited.1 For that reason, regularly reviewing account activity and limiting user access can help reduce potential risk. In addition, cash flow management is a key consideration. Understanding how money moves in and out of a business supports overall stability.2 Even simple tracking practices can provide helpful visibility. Improving efficiency as activity increases As a business grows, transaction volume often rises. At this stage, efficiency becomes just as important as access. Processes that once worked may begin to slow operations or create unnecessary complexity. As a result, many businesses look for ways to streamline routine tasks. Efficiency is not only about reducing costs. It is also about reducing manual effort and saving time. For example, tools such as automated payments and digital deposits can help simplify workflows. Similarly, clearer approval steps can reduce delays. Together, these changes can help teams focus more on day-to-day operations. Managing payment timing and cash flow In addition to efficiency, payment timing can have a direct impact on liquidity. When funds are received or sent can influence how a business manages its daily operations. Because of this, faster payment options may become more relevant over time. These options can help improve flexibility and responsiveness.3 However, it is still important to balance speed with predictability. Reviewing payment timing alongside cash flow needs can help businesses determine what approach fits best with their operations. Strengthening receivables and payment processes As activity increases, receivables often become more complex. A larger customer base typically results in more invoices and follow-up. At the same time, delayed payments can reduce visibility and make planning more difficult. Over time, this may impact overall predictability. For these reasons, reviewing receivables processes can be helpful. This includes how invoices are issued, tracked, and reconciled. In many cases, improving these steps can help reduce administrative strain while also supporting more consistent cash flow. Introducing treasury visibility and tools As operations expand, many businesses look for greater visibility into their finances. At this stage, treasury management becomes more relevant. Treasury management goes beyond individual transactions. Instead, it focuses on understanding overall cash position, improving working capital and maintaining control across accounts. With that in mind, businesses may consider tools that provide reporting and centralized visibility. These tools can support more informed decision-making as complexity increases. Adding structure with stronger controls As teams grow and responsibilities expand, financial activity becomes more complex. Because of this, stronger internal controls may become necessary over time. These controls often include clearer role definitions, structured approval workflows, and regular account reviews. Together, they can help support accuracy and reduce the risk of errors. In addition, establishing consistent processes can improve transparency across teams. As a result, businesses are better positioned to maintain oversight as they scale. Strengthening security as risk evolves As businesses become more complex, exposure to security risks may increase. More users, systems, and devices can create additional points of access. Because of this, reviewing security practices on a regular basis can be helpful. This may include updating passwords, reviewing user permissions, monitoring device access, and educating employees on how to properly respond to external requests or fraudulent attempts to access financial or banking information. The FTC highlights the importance of protecting sensitive information, particularly when using shared or public systems.4 As a result, strengthening these practices can help reduce risk over time. Preparing for disruptions and continuity While growth creates opportunities, it can also introduce new challenges. Disruptions can happen unexpectedly, which may affect access to systems or funds. For that reason, planning ahead can help reduce potential impact. Having contingency plans in place can support continued operations when needed. This may include identifying alternative payment methods or maintaining backup processes. More broadly, having a plan in place can help ensure continuity when timing matters most.5 Making financial reviews an ongoing practice Ultimately, business growth is not always linear. Financial needs continue to evolve as operations change. For that reason, regular financial reviews can help ensure alignment. Revisiting areas such as cash management, controls, and security can support long-term stability. By approaching these reviews as an ongoing process, businesses can adapt more effectively. Over time, this can help support both day-to-day operations and future growth. Our team at Byline Bank is here to help you navigate the financial needs that come with business growth. Whether you are revisiting cash flow, payment processes, or internal controls, we can help you explore solutions that align with your current stage and goals.
